summary: Sudden uptick in server errors traced to slow DNS resolution and aggressive runtime retry loops
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-10T09:12Z we observed a rapid increase in 5xx error responses for a single enterprise tenant (Acme Retail) across multiple routes. Users reported failed streaming connections and aborted generation calls. Impact: ~18% error rate on tenant routes for ~30 minutes, elevated tail latency and multiple runtime worker restarts on the serving pool. Scope: Customer-facing API gateway returned 502/504 and the serving-runtime processes logged repeated connection timeouts followed by watchdog restarts. Hypothesis at triage: upstream DNS resolution delays caused connection setup timeouts which triggered immediate retry logic in the edge proxy and runtime, amplifying load and causing worker churn.
reproduction_steps: 1) Run bulk client traffic against tenant API key with streaming enabled (simulated load used: 600 concurrent short sessions).
2) Introduce artificial DNS latency by delaying responses for model-hosting endpoints (test used: dnsproxy with 250-800ms delay).
3) Observe gateway metrics: inflight requests, retry count, and 5xx rate.
4) Tail serving-runtime logs to observe TLS handshake timeouts and watchdog restarts.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:12:18Z apigw[edge-12] WARN tenant=acme route=/v1/chat 502 upstream: connection timed out after 200ms
2026-03-10T09:12:21Z edge-proxy[proxy-3] INFO retry=1 route=/v1/stream tenant=acme upstream_connect_ttfb=340ms
2026-03-10T09:12:25Z runtime[svr-44] ERROR tls: handshake timeout (connect) to model-host-10.2.1.23:443
2026-03-10T09:12:27Z runtime[svr-44] WARN watchdog: restart triggered due to repeated connect timeouts
2026-03-10T09:14:00Z apigw[edge-12] ERROR rate: 18.3% 5xx over 5m window for tenant=acme
investigation_notes: SRE correlated the 5xx spike with an increase in DNS lookup latency from our internal resolvers to the model-host zone: median resolution increased from 12ms to 260ms between 09:10-09:20Z.
Packet captures show SYN/TCP handshake succeeded but TLS handshake stalled waiting for remote response; application saw repeated connect timeouts (~200-350ms).
Connection pool metrics: active TCP connections per runtime worker increased by 3x, queued handshakes rose, and per-worker file descriptor usage hit soft limits on some hosts.

Edge proxy retry policy triggered immediate retries (max_retries=2, backoff=linear short). Retries were not jittered and occurred while DNS resolution remained slow, amplifying concurrent TLS attempts.
DNS provider (third-party) reported transient hiccup for the model-hosting zone at 09:08-09:22Z; internal caching TTLs were low for these hosts which increased resolver load.
No evidence of model-serving OOMs; runtime restarts originated from the watchdog detecting repeated handshake/connect timeouts rather than memory faults.
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10T09:30Z: Customer reports streaming sessions failing with 502 and clients seeing ‘connection reset by peer’. Opened incident and escalated to SRE.

SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-10T09:40Z: We see DNS latency spike to model-host zone; flagging DNS provider. Pausing aggressive retries at edge via a temporary config change (decrease retries to 0 for tenant routes) to reduce amplification.
Customer (Acme Retail - Sarah Liu) 2026-03-10T09:47Z: Thank you — reducing retries seems to have improved error rate from 24% -> 6% within 4 minutes.

Runtime Eng (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-10T10:05Z: Observed fewer watchdog restarts after edge retry reduction. Preparing a hotfix to add exponential backoff + jitter and a DNS-failure slow-path to reduce parallel handshakes.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-12T15:12Z: Confirmed with customer that behavior returned to baseline and provided incident summary and credit offer. Ticket moved to Resolved.
resolution: Applied temporary mitigation: disabled immediate retries for affected tenant at edge and increased internal DNS caching TTL for model-host zone. Deployed runtime hotfix (PR #4163) implementing exponential backoff + jitter on connect retries and a DNS failure slow-path that limits parallel handshake attempts. DNS provider resolved transient degradation. Customer error rate returned to baseline within 10 minutes after mitigations.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem: publish full incident postmortem to ops runbook and link on Confluence (owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2026-03-18).
2) Deploy permanent edge config change: default retry policy to use exponential backoff with jitter for all tenant routes (owner: Edge team, PR referenced above).
3) Add circuit-breaker in runtime to cap concurrent handshakes per worker when DNS failures detected (owner: Runtime team).
4) Engage with DNS provider for root-cause and SLA review; consider additional resolver redundancy (owner: NetOps).
5) Communicate final postmortem and applied credits to Acme Retail (owner: Customer Success).
